beats.trigger: ## Lecture: Access is not absorption
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: Access is a switch somebody flips, and it completes in a minute. Absorption happens in other people's weeks, at their pace, for their reasons.
beats.got: Licences get counted as if they were adoption. It is the same mistake as with our learning portal, and I can bring it to leadership as one clear line.

beats.trigger: Companies, even when they go agentic, work first and foremost on the human principle.
beats.got: A good agent analysis still died because leadership had not done the work themselves and nobody owned the decision. That is a people problem, not a tool problem. It also quietly says that replacing headcount is not the first thing that happens.

beats.trigger: organisations of every size are working out how best to approach it.

beats.trigger: Somebody they trust has to have used it first and said so.
beats.got: Spread goes through trusted people and through where the person already looks, not through a rollout. That is how a habit moves from one person to a team.

beats.trigger: Have the conversation before you build anything more.
beats.got: Talk to the person before building more.

take_homes: Access is not adoption. A licence count says nothing about whether people use the agent, and I can take that to the leadership team.
Start from the colleague's job and what they use today, and ask what would have to be true for them to switch. Do not start from my tool.
A people plan with unnamed roles means the rollout is not ready. Someone has to own, govern and judge it.

monday.move: Ask one HR business partner how she builds the weekly people-metrics summary today, and what would make her trust an agent-made one. Build nothing yet.
monday.who: One HR business partner from my team
monday.stop_condition: If she says she would not use it, or if employee data is needed, I stop and take it to the DPO and the employee representatives before going further.
monday.blocker: Employee data in an AI tool needs the works council and the DPO, and I have not asked either of them yet. The module never mentions this.

misconception.why: The story shows that even a good agent-made analysis stalled on people and decisions, and the module keeps asking who owns things. I still think roles will change, and the module does not say which. But it made me less sure that headcount is the first thing to go. Leadership was the first to stall, not the workers.

one_line: Good on why rollouts stall and on starting with one named person. It says nothing about works councils or GDPR, and the generic 'context' slides could go.
